item.title: Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigeria and three neighbouring countries — Cameroon, Chad and Niger — have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders. The arrangement is aimed at strengthening regional counterterrorism operations and preventing fleeing militants from escaping military pressure by crossing into neighbouring territories. The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed the agreement in Abuja, explaining that it would enable security forces to sustain hot pursuit of fleeing terrorists across border areas. The agreement is expected to strengthen military cooperation among the four countries, particularly in tackling transnational security threats posed by Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and other armed criminal groups operating around the Lake Chad Basin and adjoining border communities. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was receiving real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training support from the United States to enhance its counterterrorism capabilities and improve the effectiveness of military operations. The Defence Minister said Nigerian troops had recently neutralised several terrorist and bandit commanders during overnight operations across the North-East and North-West regions. He said the cross-border pursuit arrangement is particularly significant for communities along Nigeria’s borders with Cameroon, Chad and Niger, where terrorist groups have exploited porous boundaries to evade security operations and sustain their activities. In Cameroon’s Far North Region, Boko Haram and ISWAP activities have continued to pose security challenges, making closer military coordination between neighbouring countries critical to addressing the threat. Details of the agreement, including its operational procedures, rules of engagement and safeguards for civilians in affected border communities, have not been provided in the information released. The arrangement signals a renewed push for regional military cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations against terrorist networks whose activities extend beyond national boundaries. The post Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gun can kill terrorists, only education can kill terrorism – Buratai
item.description: The former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai has called for inclusive education and wider access to learning opportunities, saying they are critical to addressing the conditions that sustain terrorism and violent extremism in Nigeria. Buratai made the call at the 2026 Young Adult Literature Prize Award and unveiling of the 2025 anthology of the T.Y. Buratai Literary Initiative (TYBLI), on Wednesday in Nasarawa State. The former Nigerian Ambassador to Benin Republic said military force alone could not defeat terrorism without deliberate investment in education, intellectual development and the minds of young Nigerians. “Gun can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism,” he declared. Buratai said national development must go beyond infrastructure, military strength and economic resources to include the intellectual capacity, creative imagination and moral consciousness of citizens. He stressed that young Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds, needed equal opportunities, platforms and encouragement to develop their talents and contribute meaningfully to society. The former COAS said the initiative was established on the conviction that great nations were built not only by strong armies and economies but also by ideas, literature and educated citizens. He urged universities to promote young adult literature through research, teaching and programmes that encouraged creativity, critical thinking and intellectual development. “A school that produces excellent academic results but neglects imagination and critical thinking has not fully prepared its students for the future,” he said. Buratai said the initiative had, since 2023, provided a platform for young Nigerians from diverse backgrounds to demonstrate their creativity and move from passive consumption to active production of literature. He described the unveiling of the 2025 anthology as another milestone, providing a permanent record of the imagination, creativity and achievements of young authors. He also announced plans to introduce full scholarships for deserving winners within the next three to five years, to enable them to complete their education. In a goodwill message, the Vice-Chancellor of Nasarawa State University, Keffi, Prof. Sa’adatu Liman, described young adult literature as an important bridge between childhood and adulthood. Liman said literature helped young people confront questions of identity, courage, faith, justice and leadership through stories that reflected their experiences. She described the initiative as an investment in human development and nation-building, pledging the university’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with TYBLI. Also, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, commended the initiative for recognising the importance of academic leadership, scholarship and research mentorship. item.title: FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent to media houses by Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Wednesday night, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. The post FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu hails Alake of Egbaland’s 21-year reign
item.description: ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎President Bola Tinubu has paid tribute to the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, describing his 21 years on the throne as a testament to selfless service and dedication to his people’s welfare. ‎ ‎The President in a tribute marking the monarch’s anniversary, praised his commitment to development, cultural preservation and responsible leadership. ‎ ‎“Your Majesty, 21 years on the throne is no ordinary milestone. It is a remarkable testament to your selfless service and dedication to your people’s welfare,” the President said. ‎ ‎Tinubu saluted the monarch’s military career before his ascension, highlighting the principles that defined his service to the nation. ‎ ‎“Your Majesty, your journey to the revered throne was preceded by your distinguished and illustrious military career, where discipline, courage, patriotism, loyalty, and a deep sense of duty formed the core of your guiding principles in serving the nation.” ‎ ‎The President said the Alake’s reign had witnessed development within the Egba kingdom and across the state, underscoring the contribution of traditional institutions to governance and development. ‎ ‎“For 21 remarkable years, your reign has witnessed tremendous development, not only within the Egba kingdom but also across the state. ‎ ‎”These strides in development stand as enduring reminders of the invaluable role of the traditional institution in complementing governments of the day for overall development.” ‎ ‎Tinubu also commended the monarch’s dedication to preserving cultural heritage and acknowledged the influence of his counsel on elected leaders. ‎ ‎“Your unwavering commitment to preserving and promoting our rich cultural heritage deserves commendation and emulation across all strata,” he said. ‎ ‎“Your words of advice, with consistent emphasis on responsible leadership, humility, accountability, service to the people, and respect for institutions, continue to guide us as elected leaders of the people.” ‎ ‎Congratulating the sons and daughters of Egbaland, the President said God had answered their prayers for a king distinguished by wisdom, humility and dedication to service. ‎ ‎“As you celebrate this remarkable anniversary, I congratulate the sons and daughters of Egbaland that Almighty God answered their prayers for a King filled with wisdom, dedication to service, humility and whose reign will be known for peace and development.” ‎ ‎The President concluded his tribute with prayer, saying: “May Almighty God grant Your Majesty sound health, renewed strength, divine wisdom and many more fruitful and peaceful years on the throne.” The post Tinubu hails Alake of Egbaland’s 21-year reign appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Air strikes kill 21 ISWAP terrorists in Borno
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi In a significant operational success, precision air strikes conducted by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), between 16 and 17 November 2026, have neutralised 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and severely injured 10 others in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State. A statement signed by Captain Mohammed Goni, Acting Military Information Officer, said, “The first operation followed intelligence reports of ISWAP fighters advancing towards Monguno. “Acting on the intelligence, an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) established surveillance over the area and identified terrorists moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno. “The subsequent precision strike neutralised seven fighters, including members of the terrorist group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network. Further confirmation revealed that Abba Bomma, identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries. “In a separate operation at Arinna in the South Lake Chad area, precision air strikes dealt a significant blow to ISWAP’s leadership and operational structure. Among those neutralised was Malkam Sharki, a prominent member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander). “Also neutralised was ABU SAAD, the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu. Twelve additional fighters were eliminated, while five others sustained severe injuries. Several terrorist motorcycles were also destroyed during the operation. “Altogether, the two operations accounted for 21 ISWAP fighters neutralised and 10 severely injured. “The strikes have significantly degraded the group’s leadership structure, disrupted its IED network and weakened its operational capabilities. “The Theatre Command reaffirms its resolve to maintain sustained operational pressure on terrorists until lasting peace and normalcy are restored across the North East. “Residents are encouraged to continue supporting security agencies with credible and timely information.” The post Air strikes kill 21 ISWAP terrorists in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Tejuosho for alleged N603.4m job scam
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday arraigned a socialite, Halimat Adenike Tejuosho, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Gwagwalada Division, for an alleged N603,400,000.00 job scam. She was arraigned before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining by false pretence and criminal conduct, according to a statement posted on EFCC’s X page. Count one reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho and Gidado Ibrahim between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court obtained the sum of N603,400,000.00 (Six hundred and three million four hundred thousand naira) from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye under the false pretence that you will facilitate her appointment as the Group Managing Director, GMD of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), which pretence you knew to be false and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 1(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006 and punishable under Section 1(3) of the same Act. Count two reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N259,900,000 (Two Hundred and Fifty-Nine Million, Nine Hundred Thousand Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act. Count four states: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho on 30th September 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N50,000,000 (Fifty Million Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069 and name HALEEMS INTEGRATED SERVICES LIMITED, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act.” Tejuosho pleaded not guilty to all the charges. Following the plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, urged the court to grant the defendant bail on liberal terms, noting that all five counts are bailable offences. He said the application was anchored mainly on her ill health, citing a medical report which, he argued, showed that she was critically ill. “The ill health of an accused person is a consideration worthy enough to be reckoned as a ground of special circumstances,” he said, urging Justice Adepoju to exercise his discretion in the defendant’s favour. item.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
item.description: By Chioma Obinna Health experts on Wednesday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos, tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. item.title: How residents killed BEDC staff for disconnecting building over N300k electricity bill
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE management of the BEDC Electricity Plc on Wednesday called on the security agencies and government to ensure that its 38 years old staff identified as Oscar Nduka Eze who was brutally killed while on duty on Monday gets justice. Eze was reportedly stabbed to death around Idumobi Umunede in the Agbor Unit, Delta State after he disconnected a building said to be owing about N300,000 electricity bill. Shortly after he disconnected the building, he was said to have been trailed to a nearby house by some people suspected to have been from previous place he had gone to work when they reportedly pounced on him and stabbed him severally till he died. Addressing journalists at the company’s office, Acting Managing Director of the company, Jonathan Lawani said the killers wanted to conceal their act but unknown to them, the building which they took him to had security camera. He said “Eze went to work on Monday 16th November 2026 for his official duty to earn a legitimate living. However, at about 12 noon of that same day while he was carrying out his official work along the Idumobi by Umunede within the Agbor Business Unit of our operations in Delta State, some hoodlums, some men who claim to be more powerful than God, who has the power to take life, traced him to a house within the same community and they stabbed him with knife until he died on the spot. Caught on CCTV “What they planned did not work. These people had planned to kill him without any evidence. And what they did was to push him into a compound, a very isolated place where he went to carry out another assignment. Unfortunately for them, that house has a CCTV camera and they were all captured directly. “The simple reason for this is that this officer had disconnected their house for non-payment. The only instrument that have been approved by NERC, the Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission to ask for payment or to demand payment for those who refuse to pay us for our monthly electricity. I want to put it straight that what the late Oscar did was an approved and official assignment. “The house in question owes us almost three hundred thousand naira and he disconnected them for non-payment and left the place quietly.” Lawani said Eze just got married four months ago after his wife died. He said five persons have been arrested in connection to the incident. “We cannot bring him back but we must ensure that justice is served. We will do everything in line with the law to see that justice is served,” he added. item.title: PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe In a significant demonstration of political tolerance, sportsmanship and solidarity, the Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has paid a solidarity visit to leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who sustained injuries in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally on Tuesday. The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of its Campaign Council, Hon. Dan’azumi Adamu Pindiga, visited the injured APC leaders at the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to express sympathy and wish them a speedy recovery. Those involved in the accident included the APC State Campaign Council Director-General, Hon. Sa’adu Hassan, and the Gombe State APC Chairman, Hon. Dantata Ndus, alongside other party members. Members of the PDP delegation included the party’s State Secretary, Hon. Adamu Abubakar; Hon. Abubakar Walama; Hon. Sani Hassan Dogarai; Hon. Hassan Santana; Hon. Abubakar Bello (Cikasoron Gombe); and Hon. Jalo Ahmed Ganga. During the visit, Pindiga conveyed messages of solidarity and goodwill on behalf of the PDP leader in Gombe State, former Governor, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, OON, PhD, Talban Gombe; the party’s governorship candidate, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; and the entire PDP family in the state. The delegation also offered prayers to Almighty Allah to grant the injured party chieftains and other victims of the accident complete healing, renewed strength and a speedy recovery. Speaking during the visit, the PDP representatives stressed that political differences should not undermine the bonds of brotherhood, humanity and mutual respect among the people of Gombe State. They maintained that, “beyond party affiliations and electoral interests, political actors remain members of one community with shared responsibilities and a common obligation to promote peaceful coexistence”. According to the delegation, “an unfortunate incident involving members of another political party should attract the concern and sympathy of all, irrespective of political leanings”. The visit, coming amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscores the need for political maturity, tolerance and civility among competing parties and their supporters. It also sends a strong message that political competition should be anchored on issues, policies and the contest for public support, rather than hostility, animosity or division. The PDP delegation reiterated its goodwill towards the injured APC leaders and prayed for their full recovery, stressing that humanity must always take precedence over partisan considerations. According to them, “Politics Should Never Come Before Humanity; We Are All Brothers and sisters”. item.title: US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash
item.description: An American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian users over her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London interviewed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday and was subsequently photographed with the President and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila. Following the interview, she published several posts on X expressing support for the Nigerian government’s security cooperation with the United States. In one of the posts, London described the US-Nigeria security partnership as one that was “delivering results”, crediting Tinubu and US President Donald Trump for their commitment to tackling terrorism. “The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote. She also described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, expressing optimism that the relationship could create additional economic and trade opportunities for both countries. In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on initiatives relating to the protection of religious groups and strengthening relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. However, the posts were subsequently deleted from her X account amid criticism from Nigerian social media users over her engagement with the Tinubu administration. The controversy followed a report by Peoples Gazette alleging that London received $4.5 million for the interview assignment. The allegation generated reactions on social media, with some users questioning the reported payment and the nature of the engagement. Checks on her X account on Wednesday showed that access to the comment section had been restricted, with a notice indicating that only selected accounts could respond to her posts. Before the restriction, some users had questioned her decision to delete the posts praising the Nigerian government’s security partnership with the United States. London had not publicly explained the deletion of the posts or the restriction of comments as of the time of filing this report. item.title: 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari
item.description: …Niger leads rice, yam production — NAERLS report By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has said increased food production during the 2026 wet season has contributed to a reduction in food prices despite persistent challenges in the agricultural sector. Kyari spoke on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Agricultural Performance Survey Report by the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS), Professor Yusuf Sani, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. The minister said the report indicated an increase in agricultural output compared with 2025, attributing the development to government interventions aimed at boosting food production and improving affordability. He cited reductions in the prices of commodities such as garri and millet, saying the trend reflected improvements in food supply. “When you do comparison between 2025 and 2026, I am not even comparing 2023 and 2026, just within the one year, we have seen prices dropping — garri, millet, and so on and so forth, that has come down,” he said. Kyari added that another harvest was expected within the next month, which he said could further improve food availability. On agricultural mechanisation, he said deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within the next two to three months. He also disclosed that the Federal Government planned to release food commodities stored under the Guaranteed Minimum Price (GMP) programme through the Bank of Agriculture to help stabilise market prices. “That is also in the works, and very soon we will announce how the methodology of that release will be made,” he said. On fertiliser supply, Kyari said the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative planned to release three million bags of fertiliser within one month to reduce input costs for farmers. He said the programme, announced by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, was part of efforts to improve agricultural productivity and balance the interests of farmers, processors and consumers. The minister also pointed to increased private-sector investment in agricultural processing, particularly in cocoa, sesame, soybean and shea nut. He said investments by multinational companies in the country’s agricultural sector indicated growing confidence in Nigeria’s business environment. Kyari further disclosed that $33 million had been invested in the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) programme. He said government interventions over the past three years had contributed to increased productivity across several crop categories, although some crops continued to record declines. Presenting the survey findings, NAERLS Executive Director, Professor Yusuf Sani, said Niger State emerged as the country’s leading producer of rice and yam. item.title: Naira weakens to N1,470/$ at parallel market
item.description: The naira depreciated to N1,470 per dollar at the parallel foreign exchange market on Wednesday, its weakest performance since January 28. The latest rate represented a N25, or 1.73 per cent, decline from the N1,445 per dollar quoted on Tuesday. Currency traders, popularly known as Bureau De Change operators, in Lagos quoted the buying rate at N1,450 per dollar and the selling rate at N1,470. The local currency had traded at N1,430 per dollar on Monday, compared with N1,390 on November 13, representing a depreciation of N40, or 2.88 per cent. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official window, the naira also weakened to N1,363.23 per dollar. Data from the NFEM showed that the currency depreciated by N7.43, or 0.55 per cent, from the N1,355.80 per dollar recorded on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $43.64 billion as of November 14, compared with $45.56 billion recorded on January 2. The figures, obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), indicated a decline of $1.92 billion, or 4.21 per cent, in the country’s external reserves since the beginning of the year. In a related development, the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) on Wednesday signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, energy financing and macroeconomic stability. item.title: NNPC, CBN sign deal to boost oil production to 3m bpd
item.description: By Udeme Akpan The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve financial discipline and attract investment into the country’s energy sector. The agreement, signed at the CBN headquarters in Abuja on Wednesday, is also expected to support NNPC’s ambition to increase Nigeria’s crude oil production from the current 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day. Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr. Bashir Bayo Ojulari, described the agreement as a defining moment in the relationship between the national oil company and the country’s monetary authority. He said the MoU established a structured framework for collaboration between both institutions at the intersection of energy and finance. “This MoU provides that structure by which the two institutions will collaborate at the meeting point between energy and finance,” Ojulari said. He explained that the partnership would support NNPC’s initiatives, strengthen the flow of export proceeds into the Nigerian economy, address foreign exchange challenges affecting trade and improve financing arrangements for energy projects. According to him, the agreement would also help the company raise capital based on its balance sheet and assets, with guidance from the CBN. “We are here to build a working partnership that delivers results,” he said. Providing further details, NNPC’s Group Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Adedapo Segun, said the agreement would replace previous practices of addressing financial issues through irregular arrangements with a more coordinated and structured approach. He explained that improved coordination between the two institutions would help attract the investment required to raise crude oil production from 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day. On implementation, Segun said NNPC would align domestic payments, contractor settlements and foreign exchange conversions with CBN regulations to support the stability of the naira and reduce dollarisation. He added that both institutions had agreed to establish working groups, implementation timelines and accountability mechanisms to ensure effective execution of the MoU. The Treasurer of NNPC Limited, Mr. John Etukudo, will oversee implementation on behalf of the company. On his part, the CBN Governor, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, described the agreement as a formalisation of an existing relationship between the two institutions. item.title: Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite the implementation of recommendations made by the independent investigative committee into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State. The lawmakers specifically called for accountability, appropriate sanctions against officers found culpable and institutional reforms within the NSCDC, warning that further delay in implementing the recommendations could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to justice. The Senate also stressed the need for prompt payment of financial compensation recommended for the families of the deceased. The resolutions followed a motion on Wednesday sponsored by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Sani Musa (APC, Niger East), and co-sponsored by 18 other senators from the North-Central geopolitical zone and Senator Nasir Sani Zango Daura (APC, Katsina North). The Senate commended President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government for establishing an independent investigative committee to probe the incident and acknowledged that the 10-member panel, chaired by Jonathan Kure, had submitted its report. The committee reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the victims’ families and other affected persons. The lawmakers recalled that the 37 miners died on September 17, 2026, while in NSCDC custody in Minna, Niger State, after reportedly being arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities. They expressed concern that the circumstances surrounding the deaths raised serious questions about the protection of fundamental human rights and the responsibility of security agencies to safeguard persons in their custody. The Senate warned that any further delay in implementing the committee’s recommendations, particularly the payment of compensation, would prolong the suffering of the bereaved families. It also called for comprehensive reforms in the management of detention facilities and the operational procedures of security agencies to prevent a recurrence. Seconding the motion, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy, insisting that the circumstances of the deaths should be examined objectively, irrespective of the alleged activities of the deceased. He said: “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing.” Nwoko, who drew parallels with incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities in oil-producing communities in the South-South, said the country must apply consistent standards in addressing such cases. He added: “The fact that some of these young men may have been involved in illegal activities should not mean that their lives are not valued. “Life is life, regardless of the circumstances. item.title: 2027: APM governorship candidate mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Laja Adeoye, has expressed sadness over the death of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, popularly known as Femi Ajasa, Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited. Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. Adeoye, who disclosed this in a condolence statement on Wednesday, described the late journalist as a professional who demonstrated passion, integrity and commitment to truth in the discharge of his duties. He said Ajasa approached journalism with dedication and professionalism, adding that his contributions to Vanguard and the wider media industry would not be forgotten. The APM governorship candidate, who described himself as an advocate of press freedom, said a free and responsible press remained indispensable to democracy. He noted that journalists like Ajasa embodied the values that made press freedom meaningful, pledging his continued support for media practitioners and the protection of press freedom. Adeoye said the deceased would be greatly missed by his colleagues at Vanguard, members of the Nigerian media community and all those who knew and worked with him. He extended his condolences to Ajasa’s family, friends and the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, praying God to grant them the strength to bear the loss and for the repose of the deceased’s soul. item.title: Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professional training. Tinubu announced the approval in a speech delivered by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The President said a major outcome of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum was the determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession. He said: “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.” He described the proposed institution as a major investment in human capital and the future of communication, adding that it would provide opportunities to develop communication leaders capable of responding to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. Tinubu commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, and the Nasarawa State Government for their collaboration and commitment to the initiative. He urged stakeholders to work together to ensure that the institution developed into a centre of excellence. The President also expressed Nigeria’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the international public relations community for entrusting the country with the hosting of the global gathering. He described the decision as recognition of Nigeria’s growing contribution to the global communication profession and its capacity to promote responsible communication. Tinubu said hosting the forum provided an opportunity to showcase Nigeria’s people, cultural diversity, economic potential and commitment to constructive international engagement. Addressing the changing communication landscape, the President said digital technologies and artificial intelligence were transforming how information was created, distributed and consumed. He, however, warned that the developments had also created challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and declining public trust. “In this environment, public relations and communication professionals have responsibilities that go beyond managing images and reputations,” he said. According to him, communication professionals must promote truth, accountability, transparency, mutual understanding and constructive engagement between governments, institutions and citizens. item.title: Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest
item.description: The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction. The coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, resumed proceedings after the High Court dismissed an application by Euracare Hospital seeking to stop the inquest. At Wednesday’s sitting, Taiwo Osipitan, counsel to Euracare Hospital, said it was the first time all parties were appearing before the coroner following the conclusion of proceedings at the High Court. Osipitan said the High Court had ruled that the matter had not reached the stage at which judicial review was necessary and directed that the case be returned to the coroner’s court for continuation of the inquest. He subsequently tendered a copy of the High Court judgment before Adetunji. However, Chukwudi Enebeli, counsel to the deceased’s family, told the court that Euracare’s application was struck out because the coroner’s court had jurisdiction to proceed with the inquest. Enebeli sought an adjournment, explaining that Euracare had only served the parties in open court with the witness statement on oath of Tosin Majekodunmi, a medical doctor. He said the family needed time to examine the statement and determine whether a response would be necessary. Abiodun Loyonu, counsel to Atlantis Paediatric Hospital, also asked the court for an opportunity to respond to Euracare’s witness statement. In her response, the magistrate reminded the parties that the inquest was inquisitorial in nature, adding that guidelines for conducting the proceedings had been discussed at a preliminary meeting held at the commencement of the inquiry. She urged all parties to bear the distinctive nature of the proceedings in mind as the inquest progressed. The coroner also asked whether the parties had filed witness statements on oath in preparation for the hearing. Osipitan, however, sought clarification on whether Lagos State Government officials would be required to file witness statements on oath or could appear in court to give oral evidence if subpoenaed. Adetunji said filing witness statements on oath was not mandatory for such witnesses, adding that government officials summoned through subpoenas could appear before the court and give oral evidence. The parties subsequently agreed that the deceased’s family would lead evidence, followed by Atlantis Paediatric Hospital and Euracare Hospital. The coroner adjourned the inquest to January 19, 20 and 28, 2027. Nkanu, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures at Euracare Hospital after being referred from Atlantis Paediatric Hospital. item.title: ADC campaign accuses INEC of bias, demands postponement of mock election test
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement. The Council said the short notice would make it difficult for parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for the nationwide exercise, warning that the process could undermine confidence in a test designed to assess electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC also faulted INEC’s reported decision not to upload results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, during the 2027 elections. The Council said INEC’s November 16 notification, coming barely two days before the November 18 deadline for submitting agents’ names, was unfair, particularly as the exercise would cover all 774 Local Government Areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas. “How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the Council queried. “INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.” It demanded an immediate postponement to give political parties sufficient time to nominate agents and participate meaningfully. On electronic transmission of results, the ADC-PCC rejected comments reportedly made by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the system for uploading results from the various collation levels. “Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels. “Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation,” the Council warned. It recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had promised to extend result uploads to Ward, Local Government and State levels, adding that his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also pledged to strengthen electoral transparency. Questioning the Commission’s apparent change of position, the ADC-PCC asked: “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians?” It further questioned why Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) could not be uploaded to IReV when the Commission already had the technology to upload polling-unit results on Form EC8A. item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked. item.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
item.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world.
